subject: Chemistry
title: Pressure Cookers and Boiling Points
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Pressure Cookers and Boiling Points.

hook.text: A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water to 120°C. Food cooks in a third of the normal time.

buildup.text: Water boils at 100°C at sea level. But at higher pressure, molecules need more energy to escape as steam.

discovery.text: The sealed pot traps steam, raising internal pressure to about 1 atmosphere above normal.

twist.text: At high altitude, pressure is lower and water boils below 100°C. On Everest, water boils at just 70°C—you can't brew tea.

climax.text: Denis Papin invented the pressure cooker in 1679. He called it the 'steam digester.' It inspired the steam engine.

punchline.text: More pressure, higher boiling point, faster cooking. Physics serves dinner.

quiz.question: Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker?
options: Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water, increasing cooking temperature
The steam adds extra calories of heat
The sealed environment prevents nutrients from escaping

details.summary: Pressure cookers raise the boiling point of water by increasing atmospheric pressure inside a sealed vessel. At 15 psi above atmospheric, water boils at 121 degrees Celsius instead of 100, cooking food faster because the higher temperature accelerates chemical reactions exponentially.
details.whyItMatters: Pressure cooking saves energy and time by reducing cooking durations by up to 70 percent. The same principle is used in autoclaves that sterilize medical equipment and in industrial food processing.
takeaways: Increased pressure raises water's boiling point above 100 degrees Celsius
At 121°C, cooking reactions proceed roughly four times faster than at 100°C
Autoclaves use the same principle to sterilize medical instruments

faq.question: Why does higher pressure raise the boiling point of water?
faq.answer: Boiling occurs when water's vapor pressure equals atmospheric pressure. Higher external pressure means water molecules need more kinetic energy to escape as vapor. This requires higher temperatures..

faq.question: Are modern pressure cookers safe after historical reports of explosions?
faq.answer: Modern pressure cookers have multiple safety features including locking lids that prevent opening under pressure, backup pressure release valves, and gasket designs that vent before dangerous pressures build. Older models lacked these redundancies and were responsible for the explosion reputation.
